CHEMISTRY · LAUREATE 01

ASYMMETRIC CATALYSIS · NONLINEAR EFFECTS

HenriKagan.

A chemist whose work on molecular chirality showed that product handedness need not vary linearly with the handedness of a catalyst.

Start the study lensChemistry overview
ROLEOrganic chemist
CORE IDEANonlinear effects in asymmetric catalysis
IMPACTUnderstand and optimise chiral amplification

WHY HE MATTERS

Measure how chirality amplifies

Kagan’s work made nonlinear behaviour a diagnostic and design principle. By comparing catalyst enantiomeric purity with product selectivity, chemists could infer hidden aggregation and interaction effects in catalytic systems.

I
INPUT

A catalyst with partial chiral bias

The catalyst mixture contains unequal amounts of two mirror-image forms.

P
PROCESS

Nonlinear molecular interactions

Catalyst species associate or react in ways that reshape selectivity.

O
OUTPUT

Amplified product selectivity

The product’s enantiomeric excess can exceed a simple linear prediction.

THREE-PASS REVIEW

Read the contribution from three angles

ACTIVE LENS

The person

Kagan spent much of his career at Orsay studying molecular chirality and asymmetric catalysis. His work joined practical synthesis with questions about how molecular handedness emerges and grows.
